newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 10.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- More than 100 of the estimated 400 South African municipalities stand to lose their licences to supply electricity following a decision by the national electricity regulator to take action against non-performing electricity distributors.
- Foreign investors are showing signs of liking South Africa again, helping the rand to consolidate at stronger levels and underpinning bullish sentiment in the gilts market.

- The foreign affairs department has been holding discussions with other Southern African Development Community countries (SADC) on the possibility of merging overseas missions to reduce costs, SADC sources confirmed.

- Government has taken another small step towards easing foreign exchange regulations by allowing Randgold's Harmony Gold Mining Co to market a third of its own gold production on international markets.

- In another positive development for state finances, Trevor van Heerden, the commissioner for inland revenue, said that the goal to collect 1.5 billion rand in arrears taxes this tax year had already been reached by November.
- Financial services firm Coronation Holdings has attracted 750 million rand to its two unit trusts in nine months, chairman Gavan Ryan said.
- Real Africa Durolink, BoE NatWest/Moseneke & Partners and Investec have been shortlisted from 18 bidders to advise the government on the sale of Sun Air, the government-owned domestic airline.
- The mothers of two Johannesburg teenage rape victims spoke for the first time about the pain, fear and bewilderment their daughters went through the night five men burst into their Malvern home.
